definitions.explanation: To join parts together to make a complete structure or product.
To organize or structure something systematically, such as a plan or argument.

examples.japanese: {家具|かぐ}を{組|く}み{立|た}てる。
この{棚|たな}は{自分|じぶん}で{組|く}み{立|た}てなければならない。
examples.english: You have to assemble this shelf yourself.

examples.japanese: {論理|ろんり}を{組|く}み{立|た}てて{説明|せつめい}する。
examples.english: I explain by constructing a logical argument.
examples.notes: [Note: Figurative use meaning to structure an argument]

notes:
{組|く}み{立|た}てる is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) meaning to assemble or put together.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {組|く}む (to join) + {立|た}てる (to set up) → to set up by joining parts

TRANSITIVITY:
- {組|く}み{立|た}てる ({他動詞|たどうし}): to assemble
- {組|く}み{立|た}たる ({自動詞|じどうし}): to be assembled (rare)

ASPECT (ている):
{組|く}み{立|た}てている indicates an ongoing process of assembling.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {家具|かぐ}を{組|く}み{立|た}てる (assemble furniture)
- {機械|きかい}を{組|く}み{立|た}てる (assemble a machine)
- プラモデルを{組|く}み{立|た}てる (assemble a plastic model)
- {論理|ろんり}を{組|く}み{立|た}てる (construct a logical argument)

RELATED NOUN:
- {組|く}み{立|た}て: assembly; {組|く}み{立|た}て{工場|こうじょう} = assembly plant

[Register: Neutral]
